items.text: ROSS FIRE UPDATE🔥after a couple of days of more favorable weather conditions for firefighters battling the Ross Fire in North Texas, conditions are unfortunately deteriorating again. Temperatures have climbed into the 100s, while relative humidity has fallen to around 20%, creating an environment increasingly favorable for active fire behavior and fire spread. This appears to already be occurring, with a noticeable uptick in activity showing up on satellite hot-spot detection. There are also reports that structure protection operations are underway in some areas as crews continue working the fire. Unfortunately, poor fire weather conditions are expected to persist over the next week, with continued heat and dry conditions likely to keep fuels receptive to fire spread. Residents near the fire should remain alert for additional updates and be prepared to act quickly if evacuation information is issued🔥🚒

items.text: PNW THUNDERSTORMS SATURDAY⛈️🌧️⚡thunderstorm chances will increase across parts of Washington on Saturday as a cool upper-level low and associated cold front move through the region. Across western Washington, showers will become more widespread from Seattle northward tonight into Saturday morning. By Saturday afternoon, some daytime heating combined with colder air aloft could generate a few thunderstorms over the Cascades, with activity potentially extending west toward Puget Sound as a convergence zone develops. The overall thunderstorm threat is low but isolated lightning and locally gusty winds will be possible. Farther east, a low to medium chance of thunderstorms is expected Saturday across parts of the Cascades and the northern mountains. These storms are expected to be fairly scattered but the stronger storms could produce frequent lightning and gusty outflow winds around 30 mph. Thunderstorm and shower activity should diminish Saturday evening as the system shifts east. The system will also bring a noticeable cooldown, mountain showers and generally breezy conditions across the Pacific and Inland Northwest with widespread gusts of 15-30 mph possible, especially for areas including the Columbia Basin, Palouse, Spokane/Coeur d'Alene, Waterville Plateau and Wenatchee⛈️🌧️⚡

items.author: GulfCoastUpdates
items.text:
#DOLLY: ACT II? 🎥 🍿 

The remnants of #Dolly are still being tracked, and a few models are suggesting the system could potentially get its act together again late this week into next weekend.

The GFS and Canadian are shown here, but before anyone starts squeezing their hurricane supplies a little tighter… those two are pretty much outliers right now.

They’ve basically walked into the room, slapped a low pressure on the table and said, “Hear me out…”

And we’re listening. But from a safe distance. 

What makes this slightly more interesting is the Google DeepMind AI ensembles are also showing some potential for the leftover low to find better conditions and attempt to reorganize later on.

Does that mean we’re getting Dolly: Act II?

Hell if I know. It’s hurricane season and the atmosphere does whatever it wants.

For now, nothing to worry about. This is firmly in the “Hmm… let’s keep an eye on those schmuck remnants.”

We’ll watch it this week and see if more models join the party… or if the GFS and Canadian quietly delete the evidence and act like they never said a word.

items.text: FIRE WEATHER WARNINGS FOR PARTS OF CALIFORNIA🚨🔥⚡a concerning fire-weather setup is developing across a large part of the Central Coast and parts of Southern California today with multiple Fire Weather Warnings in effect due to the combination of dry lightning, extreme heat, instability and locally strong winds! For the Central Coast, a Fire Weather Warning is in effect now through 3PM for the Santa Cruz Mountains, Monterey Bay, Big Sur Coast, Salinas and Carmel Valleys, Hollister area, interior Monterey County, Santa Lucia Mountains and Los Padres National Forest. Isolated thunderstorms could produce lightning with little rainfall and erratic outflow wind gusts of 40-50 mph. Lightning could ignite new wildfires, while strong thunderstorm winds could cause both new and existing fires to spread rapidly. For SLO County, the Fire Weather Warning has been expanded to include all of San Luis Obispo County from now through 3PM due to the risk of dry lightning. Tropical moisture will bring a chance of thunderstorms with some storms capable of producing lightning with minimal rainfall and gusty, erratic winds. There is a moderate risk for frequent new fire starts from dry lightning. And, in Southern California, Fire Weather Warnings also continue through 3 PM across interior parts of Los Angeles, Ventura and Santa Barbara counties, including the Cuyama Valley, Santa Barbara County interior mountains, Ventura County mountains, the 5 Freeway Corridor, Western San Gabriel Mountains/the 14 Freeway Corridor, Eastern San Gabriel Mountains and Santa Susana Mountains. These areas are dealing with extreme heat, an exceptionally unstable atmosphere and locally gusty winds. “⚠️ A severe flooding event affected northern Nepal and Tibet on 26 August 2026.

🛰️ The Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) Rapid Mapping component has been activated [EMSR927] to map the flood extent and assess damage across four Areas of Interest.

This data visualisation shows the area around the village of Syapru Besi, Nepal and the impact of the event on built-up and roads. 

CEMS analysis indicates that, within the area shown, more than 240 buildings were destroyed, while 32 were damaged.

🌀 TROPICAL UPDATE 🌀
12 PM FRIDAY 8/28/2026

Easy come, easy go! 

Just 24 hours after forming, Dolly has already degenerated into a tropical wave and is no longer a tropical storm. Relentless wind shear did it in, and that shear is only expected to get stronger, so the remnants should continue to weaken.

There’s a very small chance Dolly’s remnants could try to regenerate next week near the Bahamas or possibly the Gulf. I’ll keep an eye on it, but at this point, it’s certainly nothing to worry about.

That wind shear has been absolutely relentless this season!

Dual slight risks across parts of the Northern Great Basin and Northern Plains tomorrow!

As an upper-level trough pushes into the Intermountain West, strong mid-level flow will overspread moderate instability across the Northern Great Basin. This favorable wind shear and strong upper-level lift will support scattered severe thunderstorms tomorrow afternoon and evening, with organized clusters and supercells bringing a primary threat for damaging wind gusts, potentially exceeding 75mph.

Farther east, scattered severe storms are also expected across the Dakotas, where upslope flow developing near a strengthening surface low will allow supercells to organize with a threat for both large hail and severe wind gusts.

items.author: EdPiotrowskiWPDE
items.text:
Many of you have asked how my hand is doing, so here’s an update!

I’m now four weeks post-surgery, and it’s healing extremely well. In fact, I haven’t had any pain for weeks. Of course, no pain doesn’t mean it’s 100% healed. Broken bones take time, so I’m still being careful and following the rules which include wearing the splint when moving around and sleeping. 

Luckily, I’ve been in great hands (no pun intended) with the Occupational Therapy team at OrthoSC These three rockstars, from left to right, are Sonya, Liz and Kathy.

Liz, in particular, has been amazing. She’s been gradually working with me to get my hand back to normal while also taking great care of the incision area to minimize scarring. I couldn’t be happier with what she’s done for me.

And maybe just as important, they play GREAT music during therapy! I actually look forward to my visits with these ladies. Thank you for taking such great care of me!

For those who don’t know how I broke it, it happened the Friday night before Mom passed away. It was an incredibly difficult and emotional time. Mom’s health was failing, Dad wasn’t doing well, and in a moment of frustration and emotion, I punched a wall.

Unfortunately, I didn’t hit drywall. I found the stud. 

The stud won.

The result was a clean break of the fifth metacarpal in my hand and, ultimately, surgery. Definitely not one of my better decisions. But four weeks later, I’m very grateful to be healing so well and especially grateful for the people helping me get back to 100%.

The Moon appears red during a lunar eclipse because sunlight passing through Earth’s atmosphere is filtered and bent into Earth’s shadow. Blue light is scattered away, while the red and orange wavelengths make it through and illuminate the Moon.

items.text: FIRE WEATHER WARNINGS FOR PARTS OF CALIFORNIA🚨🔥⚡a concerning fire-weather setup is developing across a large part of the Central Coast and parts of Southern California on Friday with multiple Fire Weather Warnings in effect due to the combination of dry lightning, extreme heat, instability and locally strong winds. For the Central Coast, a Fire Weather Warning is in effect 5AM–3PM Friday for the Santa Cruz Mountains, Monterey Bay, Big Sur Coast, Salinas and Carmel Valleys, Hollister area, interior Monterey County, Santa Lucia Mountains and Los Padres National Forest. Isolated thunderstorms could produce lightning with little rainfall and erratic outflow wind gusts of 40-50 mph. Lightning could ignite new wildfires, while strong thunderstorm winds could cause both new and existing fires to spread rapidly. For SLO County, the Fire Weather Warning has been expanded to include all of San Luis Obispo County from 5AM-3PM Friday due to the risk of dry lightning. Tropical moisture will bring a chance of thunderstorms with some storms capable of producing lightning with minimal rainfall and gusty, erratic winds. There is a moderate risk for frequent new fire starts from dry lightning. And, in Southern California, Fire Weather Warnings also continue through 3 PM Friday across interior parts of Los Angeles, Ventura and Santa Barbara counties, including the Cuyama Valley, Santa Barbara County interior mountains, Ventura County mountains, the 5 Freeway Corridor, Western San Gabriel Mountains/the 14 Freeway Corridor, Eastern San Gabriel Mountains and Santa Susana Mountains. These areas are dealing with extreme heat, an exceptionally unstable atmosphere and locally gusty winds. Lower mountain elevations and foothills could reach 100-110°F with wind gusts of 35-40 mph through favored mountain passes and corridors. There's also a low-end chance for some lightning🚨🔥⚡

items.text: FALL TEMPS TO RING IN THE ‘BER’ MONTH📉🍂🌧️❄️a notable pattern change is setting up across the Pacific Northwest and parts of the West, moving into the first week of September, bringing cooler temperatures and increased chances for precipitation! The main driver is a trough developing near the West Coast. This southward dip in the jet stream will be associated with cooler air aloft and lower atmospheric pressure, favoring cooler air being drawn southward into the region. The latest numerical guidance continues to show the Pacific Northwest has increased odds of below-normal temperatures with the cooler signal extending south through parts of the western Great Basin and into northern and central California. The trough will also strengthen onshore flow from the Pacific, allowing cooler, moisture-rich marine air to move inland. Chances for above-normal precipitation are elevated across parts of the West, with the Pacific Northwest favored to see wetter than normal conditions. This doesn't necessarily mean continuous rain or that every location will see significant rainfall. Rather, the overall pattern becomes more favorable for passing weather systems, showers and periods of wetter weather compared with what is typical. The increased cloud cover, precipitation and stronger marine influence should also help reinforce the cooler pattern. There’s also a chance for mountain snow for the Northwest. Meanwhile, it's almost the opposite story farther south and east. Strong ridging is expected to favor continued above-normal temperatures across much of the Southwest and Southern Plains📉🌧️❄️

Two weeks after the total solar eclipse, the Moon takes its turn in Earth's shadow.

On the night of August 27-28, a deep partial lunar eclipse darkens the Full Sturgeon Moon, with up to 96% of the lunar disk sliding into Earth's umbra, the dark central shadow. It falls just short of total, leaving a thin bright sliver along one edge, but the rest of the Moon will glow a deep coppery red. This is the most dramatic lunar eclipse anywhere on Earth until the total eclipse of December 31, 2028.

🔴 Greatest eclipse comes at 04:12 UTC on August 28, with the partial phase running from 02:33 to 05:52 UTC. The Americas and South America get the best views with the Moon high overhead; observers in Europe, Africa, and western Asia should find a clear western horizon as the Moon nears setting.

No equipment or eye protection needed. Just look up 🌕🔴

TROPICAL UPDATE
5:30 PM THURSDAY 8/27/2026

Tropical Storm Dolly formed earlier today, but it’s likely to be a short-lived system. Dolly will run into a wall of strong wind shear this weekend, which should quickly take its toll.

It’s highly likely Dolly will weaken and eventually degenerate into a tropical wave, bringing gusty winds and some much-needed rainfall to drought-stricken Puerto Rico.

There’s been quite a bit of talk about whether Dolly’s remnants could reorganize once they reach an area of lighter wind shear early next week. However, given how much the system is expected to be torn apart by strong wind shear this weekend, redevelopment appears very unlikely. In fact, about 95% of the models and their ensemble members show Dolly never making a comeback.

And I’m perfectly OK with that!

Elsewhere across the Atlantic, the tropics remain quiet.

items.author: GregDeeWeather
items.text:
Fall is just around the corner, but if you're in Central Florida, don't expect it to arrive quickly. 

I know the appearance of Halloween decorations in stores, PSLs & everything else pumpkin makes it seem like fall is just around the corner. 

Although meteorological fall is Sept, Oct & Nov, here in the Bay Area, we don't really start to feel "fall" until the month of October. Even then, it's really the second half of October that starts to see more noticeable reductions in temperatures & humidity levels. Highs in October usually stay in the 80s.

The real cool stuff, highs in the 70s, doesn't happen until November & lasts through the winter months. 

Until then, September doesn't usually see much, if any, "fall-like" weather, though a drop in the humidity later in the month is not unheard of, which can at least lead to cooler nights & mornings.

items.text: THE SEASONS ARE CHANGING📉🍂there is increasing confidence in a colder system bringing well-below-normal temperatures to parts of the Inland Northwest and Northern U.S. Rockies late next week into next weekend! Depending on the strength and track of the system, even some of the highest peaks of the Cascades could see light snow during this timeframe. items.author: MeteorologistChristopherNunley
items.text: TROPICAL STORM ISELLE BRINGS MOISTURE TO CALIFORNIA BEGINNING TODAY🌀🌴🌧️ ⛈️a plume of deep tropical and subtropical moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Iselle are being pulled northward into California today and especially Friday as an upper-level trough approaches the West Coast! While this is not expected to be a widespread rain event, moisture levels will increase considerably and scattered showers and storms could develop across portions of the state. Today, tropical moisture begins spreading into Central and Southern California. There is around a low to medium chance for showers across portions of Southern California, the Central Coast and Bay Area while isolated activity will also be possible farther inland. Most locations will remain dry, but brief showers, sprinkles or virga could develop almost anywhere beneath the moisture plume. Thunderstorm chances today remain low but non-zero. The combination of tropical moisture, heat and instability means an isolated heavier shower or thunderstorm cannot be completely ruled out today. Gusty and erratic winds could also occur near showers or virga. The better opportunity for precipitation arrives Friday as the approaching Pacific Northwest trough taps directly into the subtropical moisture plume. Shower chances expand northward into the Sacramento Valley where much of the Valley now has a low to medium chance for rain showers. The Sierra Nevada should have the best opportunity for meaningful precipitation with thunderstorm probabilities increasing Friday. Localized flooding is possible in the Sierra Nevada. This is a classic low-probability, potentially higher-impact setup. Most Californians probably won't see measurable rain, but any isolated thunderstorm that develops within this unusually moist and unstable environment could produce locally heavier rain, lightning and gusty winds🌀🌴🌧️ ⛈️

items.author: MattDevittWeather
items.text:
#BREAKING: Tropical Storm #Dolly has formed in the Atlantic, 4th named storm of the 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season. It's currently forecast to be short-lived. Here's the latest and what to know: 

1) Dolly was able to develop from a small window of favorable conditions, but it looks like that will quickly be coming to an end Friday into the weekend as it encounters drier air and increasing wind shear.  More shear and dry air the better…it hurts tropical systems! The official NHC (National Hurricane Center) forecast calls for this to move into the Caribbean and then dissapate / fall apart after. 

2) Over the past several days, I’ve been discussing two track possibilities from the models. Scenario #1 quickly develops a stronger system and has it turning north out to sea. Scenario #2 is a system that either struggles after developing, or never actually develops, and heads more west as a result. Recently, almost all models have been leaning toward the western track, Scenario #2. 

3) The more west it goes, land enters into the mix. First up will be the Caribbean. Leeward Islands and Puerto Rico by Sunday into Monday. Hispaniola by Monday into Tuesday. Then after the Bahamas? Cuba? The United States? All possibilities, but what will it be at that point? Even if it develops and then falls apart, some models indicate the leftovers could try to reorganize over warmer water, greater tropical moisture and lower shear. Not a guarantee, but possible down the road. Best-case scenario is an undeveloped rainmaker. 

4)Thankfully, this is nothing to stress over this early, just putting it on your radar and keeping tabs on it. 

I'll continue to keep you updated 24/7 with no hype, just the facts. Thanks everyone!
